reaction: Seeing the parts together, with blood and nerves linking their work, was satisfying.

mostWorthwhile.text: Joining the chest and lower body was most worthwhile: the diaphragm and separate routes made their positions easier to understand.

leastWorthwhile.text: Attaching the second arm felt predictable and added little after the first arm was fitted.

surprise.text: The joined regions showed that nerves, blood vessels and the food pipe cross between chest and abdomen through their own routes.

arbitrary.text: Nothing felt especially arbitrary; the named slots and goals explained the fittings, although the final combinations were the only options offered.

continue.text: I would probably continue if another chapter explored how the assembled systems work together, though more straightforward fittings alone would be less interesting.
